venue.name: Kaatza Station Museum & Archives
venue.description: Kaatza Station Museum and Archives is run by the volunteer Kaatza Historical Society in the original Canadian Pacific train station built at Lake Cowichan in 1913. Indoor rooms cover pioneer life, the local mills and the IWA forestry union, the Bell Tower and Mesachie Lake schools, the Second World War, South Asian and Japanese connections to the town, and Ts'uubaa-asatx Nation history, along with a space for rotating exhibits. The grounds hold logging equipment and rolling stock including a Shay steam locomotive, a caboose and a logging car, plus a gathering place and totem pole carved by Nuu-chah-nulth artist Joshua Watts. The archives can be seen by appointment made by email.
venue.address: 125 B South Shore Road, Lake Cowichan, BC V0R 2G0
venue.hours_notes: September to June, Tuesday to Friday, 10am to 4pm. July and August, Tuesday to Saturday, 10am to 4pm. Closed Sundays and Mondays.
venue.seasonal_notes: Summer hours run in July and August with the museum also open on Saturdays. Winter hours run September to June.

programs.name: Museum visit
programs.description: A walk in visit during opening hours. The station building holds room sized displays on pioneer life, the mailing room and general store, the mills and the IWA union, local railways, the Second World War, South Asian and Japanese heritage and Ts'uubaa-asatx Nation history, plus a rotating exhibit space. Outside on the grounds are a Shay steam locomotive, a caboose, a passenger car, a logging car and other logging equipment. Opening days change with the season, Tuesday to Friday from September to June and Tuesday to Saturday in July and August.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the rooms of an old train station looking at model rooms and buildings filled with period objects, photographs and mill and union displays. Then go outside on the grounds to walk around a steam locomotive, a caboose and a logging car loaded with logs.
programs.our_note: The opening hours are short and it is shut on Sundays and Mondays, so a mid week morning is the safe bet. Nothing about admission price, group size or booking for a group is published, so call before you plan a class around it.
programs.practical_summary: The site gives the address, opening hours, a phone number and an email, and nothing else. Washrooms, somewhere to eat, parking, step free access and price are all unstated, so one call will answer most of it.
programs.evidence: The museum contains a variety of exhibits dedicated to the history of Lake Cowichan and the forestry industry

programs.name: Bell Tower School tour, arranged ahead
programs.description: The Bell Tower School was built in 1925 and was the main school for Lake Cowichan, and part of it now stands on the museum grounds with a replica classroom inside along with other artifacts from the region. The museum says the school building is not open to visitors at the moment but that tours can be arranged if they are booked ahead. No price, group size, length or notice period is published.
programs.what_children_do: Go inside a 1925 schoolhouse and look at a classroom set up the way it was, along with other objects from the district.
programs.our_note: This one only happens if you arrange it first, since the schoolhouse is normally kept shut. Email the museum well before your date and ask how long it takes and whether it suits your age group.
programs.practical_summary: Everything practical about this is unpublished, including price, how long it runs, how many children can come and how much notice is needed. Treat the email as the starting point rather than a booking.
programs.evidence: The school is not open to visitors at this time, but tours can be arranged if booked ahead.

images.alt: A red wooden former train station with a grey shingled roof, seen from above, with a yellow switcher engine and rail cars parked on track beside it and forested mountains behind.
A black steam locomotive lettered Comox Logging and Railway Company, an orange flat car loaded with logs and a red caboose standing on track beside a gravel path.

gaps: No admission price is published anywhere on the site, for adults, children or groups. Ask what a class of children costs, and whether accompanying adults pay.
The site never mentions school groups, daycare groups or children at all, so whether it takes them and from what age is unknown rather than refused.
No group size limit, no minimum, and no notice period are published. The Bell Tower School page says a tour can be arranged if booked ahead but does not say how far ahead.
Nothing is published about washrooms, an indoor space to eat lunch, parking, bus parking, stroller access or step free access into the 1913 station building.
How long a visit takes is not stated, and there are no published start times.
The Mill Room is described as being rebuilt at a later date and a Chinese Heritage exhibit is listed as in progress, so what is actually open on the day may differ from the exhibits list.
The site's copyright line reads 2021, so some pages may not have been updated recently. The seasonal hours are written as a standing pattern rather than dated to a particular year.
Neither photograph carries real alt text on the site, only its file name, so both descriptions were written after opening the images in a browser and looking at them.
Coordinates were taken from the location data the site itself publishes in its own page source rather than from a map pin placed by us.
